title: DARPA BTO Office-Wide BAA HR001126S0003
summary: The BTO solicitation seeks biological research that can protect warfighters and create operational capabilities. The office spans AI-enabled biology, threat detection, medical countermeasures, human performance, biological manufacturing, resilient infrastructure, and sensing.
key_findings: BTO treats biology as an engineering and manufacturing domain as well as a health domain.
Research areas connect detection, countermeasures, tactical care, and human performance.
Biological production and resilient infrastructure create scale-up and supply-chain dependencies.
why_it_matters: It reveals how biological discovery becomes a national-security production, sensing, logistics, and resilience problem.
ftfn_relevance: Extends the bioeconomy topic from laboratory results into manufacturing and operational systems.
Supports monitoring dual-use infrastructure, biosecurity, and scale-up constraints.
evidence_limits: The BAA is a research-interest document, not evidence that any proposed capability works.
Sensitive or classified follow-on work may not be visible in the public record.
